reason: The goal calls for an arm framework, so I’ll join the upper arm and forearm bones first.
expectation: I expect the bones to form an elbow framework, though it may still need cartilage and other joint structures.

alternatives.reason: Cartilage and joint fluid seem useful for smooth movement, but I want to establish the bones first.

effect: The bones provide rigid supports, but still need a joint where they can turn relative to one another.
reaction: The distinction between bending bones and movement at a joint is clear.
reason: Cartilage and joint fluid are the only offered combination and seem relevant to the goal of smooth joint surfaces.
expectation: I expect them to form a smooth, lubricated joint surface, though I don't know exactly how it will attach to the bones.

effect: The cartilage covers bone ends and joint fluid helps them slide; the next goal is to join the framework and attach the muscles.
reaction: The explanation makes the smooth surfaces' purpose clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it should join the prepared surfaces to the bones.
expectation: I expect a jointed arm framework that can later receive the opposing muscles.

effect: The jointed bones can turn at the elbow, but they still need a force to move.
reaction: The distinction between allowing movement and producing it is useful.
reason: Ligaments are the only offered combination and seem likely to hold the joint together.
expectation: I expect the ligaments to stabilize the articulated bones before the muscles are attached.

effect: The ligaments stabilize the joint, and the framework has slots for the opposing muscle pulls.
reaction: The distinction between ligaments connecting bones and muscles providing pulls is clear.
reason: I'll attach the bending muscles to fill one of the framework's pull slots.
expectation: I expect the bending muscles to attach at the front pull slot, leaving the rear slot for the straightening muscles.

alternatives.reason: The straightening muscles also need attaching, but either side seems reasonable to fit first.

effect: The bending muscles are attached, and their tendons transmit a pull to the bones; the opposing muscles are still needed to straighten the elbow.
reaction: The explanation that relaxing a muscle does not push the bones back is useful.
reason: The straightening muscles are the only offered combination and should fill the remaining pull slot.
expectation: I expect the straightening muscles to attach to the rear of the framework, completing the opposing pulls.

effect: The opposing muscles complete the framework and can bend, straighten or steady the elbow; coordinating them remains another job.
reaction: Holding a weight still while muscles keep pulling was a useful addition to the model.

mostWorthwhile.text: Attaching the bending muscles was most worthwhile because it connected muscle tension to movement and explained why relaxation alone cannot push the arm back.

leastWorthwhile.text: Joining the smooth surfaces to the bones felt predictable because it was the only offered combination, though the result explained that a joint permits movement without producing force.

surprise.text: I was interested that opposing muscles can keep pulling without shortening while holding a weight still.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although several were the only offered combination and required little decision-making.

continue.text: I would choose to continue because the completed arm can move, and the mention of coordination raises a question about how those pulls are controlled. The mostly single-option steps make the assembly less engaging as a game.
